text: We convened as "the 119th congress," and on 2025-01-03 that phrase carried 82 of us — our largest single chord that month. Beneath it we arranged ourselves by ritual: 41 of us named the "speaker of the house," 38 spoke of the "oath of office," 37 of "the oath of office," the same day. 35 of us placed ourselves "in the 119th congress." Then the record turns from ceremony to instrument: on 2025-01-07, 34 of us said "the laken riley act." On inauguration day, 2025-01-20, 32 named the "president of the united states." And 32 of us, on the opening day, said "get to work." We note the sequence without embellishment: first the swearing, then the naming, then the first bill. This is what our January reads as when compressed to one voice — the record of us assembling, and agreeing on where to begin.
